instruction: Search for new language model papers from October 11, 2023 on arXiv and add at least 3 papers to the spreadsheet.

parameters.window_name: New Large Language Models.xlsx - LibreOffice Calc

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding at least 3 NEW papers from Oct 11, 2023 on arXiv about language models. Verified: Gold file has 4 rows (1 existing + 3 new from Oct 11), meeting the minimum requirement. Evaluator now checks for 3+ newly added rows with content validation.

llm_judge_reasons: Correctly counts NEW rows using baseline: Getter properly calculates new_rows_count = total_rows - baseline_rows (where baseline_rows=1), addressing the 'add at least 3 papers' requirement.

Has comprehensive content validation: Metric checks date indicators (October 11, Oct 11, 10/11, etc.), year 2023, arXiv keyword, and language model keywords (language model, llm, gpt, bert, transformer, nlp, etc.) in row content.
Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies both quantity (at least 3 new rows) and quality (papers match date, source, and topic requirements).
Proper postconfig: Saves the file before verification to ensure fresh state is read.

Minor issue - Relaxed validation logic: Uses OR logic '(has_arxiv OR (has_date AND has_2023)) AND has_lm_topic', allowing papers to pass without arXiv if they have the date, or without specific date if they have arXiv. The instruction requires papers from BOTH arXiv AND October 11, 2023, so stricter AND logic would be more accurate.
Minor issue - Keyword matching robustness: Simple substring matching could have false positives (e.g., 'arxiv' in unrelated text), though this is unlikely in practice for a spreadsheet of papers.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Strengthen validation logic to require ALL criteria: Change condition to '(has_arxiv AND has_date AND has_2023) AND has_lm_topic' to ensure papers are from arXiv AND from October 11, 2023.
Consider more robust arXiv detection: Check for arXiv URL patterns (arxiv.org) or arXiv ID format (e.g., 2310.xxxxx) in addition to keyword matching.
Add column-based validation: If the spreadsheet has structured columns (e.g., Date, Source, Title), validate specific columns rather than concatenating all cell values.
